summary: Invoice line reallocation across regions after hourly postback-label migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that their March month-to-date invoice shows a shifted set of hourly usage line items: a subset of tokens that previously billed to us-east are appearing under eu-west with zeroed reserved credits applied, and the net invoice total differs from expected by ~USD 1,320. Impact:
- Billing mismatch for StreamlineAI (enterprise); cannot reconcile month-to-date forecast with invoice.
- Customer is requesting provisional credit while we investigate; accounting flagged the discrepancy as material to their month close.
Environment:
- Production; postback ingestion is handled in us-east primary with cross-region replication.
- Affected org: org_34871 (StreamlineAI).
- Metering pipeline components: postback-processor v2, hourly-accumulator, rate-mapper service.
Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer runs steady traffic in us-east; hourly postbacks emitted to postback topic with region=us-east.
2) During a background migration on 2026-03-08 02:00 UTC, the postback-processor applied a new label normalization that rewrote region tags for certain legacy event types to eu-west when the organization had both eu and us resources.
3) Hourly-accumulator consumed these modified postbacks and attributed token counts to eu-west bucket; reserved-hour credits were applied per-region during billing aggregation.
4) Billing batch on 2026-03-09 finalized line items; resulting invoice showed split lines and a discrepancy in reserved-credit application.
Expected behavior:
- Postbacks should retain original region tag from the request origin; hourly-accumulator should not reassign region for already-labeled events. Reserved credits should remain attached to the original region’s usage.
Logs / Artifacts:
- S3: s3://redwood-metrics/postbacks/2026-03-08/postback-processor-logs-*.gz (tarball contains rewriting events for org_34871).
- Grafana dashboards: billing.hourly-accumulator.us-east, billing.hourly-accumulator.eu-west (spikes visible 2026-03-08 02:00–04:00 UTC).
- Billing export CSV: gs://billing-exports/2026-03-09/streamlineai_invoice_preview.csv
Investigation notes:
- Confirmed via postback-processor logs that a normalization rule (PR #278) incorrectly matched legacy event_type "prefixed-retry" and set region -> "eu-west" for events that had origin_region = "us-east".
- The hourly-accumulator aggregates by "region_tag" field; because the normalization mutated the tag before persistence, the accumulator had no way to link the records back to original region for reserved-credit application.
- Rate-mapper lookups later applied regional pricing tiers; eu-west pricing triggered a different reserved-credit bucket leading to an unexpected credit reallocation.
- Linked INT-4182 shows the postback-processor release was deployed as a hotfix to fix a different bug; this change was not included in release notes and lacked a migration backward-compatibility check.
- No evidence of duplicate posts (retry de-dup keys look clean). Issue appears to be reclassification rather than duplication.
Workaround / Temporary remediation:
- We recommended the customer run an interim reconciliation using the billing export CSV; Support generated a provisional CSV with corrected region tags for their accounting team.
- Engineering enabled a roll-forward: we paused the normalization rule on postback-processor and rerouted new ingestion to the pre-migration consumer group to avoid further misclassifications. This prevents new misallocated lines but does not retroactively change already-finalized invoices.
Next steps / Action items:
1) Billing team to issue a provisional credit of USD 1,320 to StreamlineAI pending final reconciliation (actioned 2026-03-11, accounting ticket ACC-9931).
2) Engineering PR to revert the normalization for legacy event types and add a region-consistency validation in the postback-processor (PR referenced above; tester: Mei Lopez).
3) Run a reprocessing job to correct historical postbacks for the affected hourly window (SRE playbook step: rehydrate from S3, apply inverse normalization, feed through accumulator in dry-run).
4) Postmortem and runbook update to require region-consistency checks in normalization steps; add automated billing preview diff alert prior to invoice finalization.
Resolution notes (interim):
- Provisional credit applied to the customer's account (see accounting memo ACC-9931).
- Postback-processor normalization disabled 2026-03-10 08:40 UTC.
- Reprocessing scheduled 2026-03-14 in a controlled window; billing will resettle and post final correction.
Reference / crosslinks:
- Slack: #support (thread t01234) and #incidents (thread t05678) discussing the customer lock.
- GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/postback-processor/pull/278
- Confluence: Hourly Accumulator Runbook and Billing Reconciliation checklist.
